title: Measuring mass and weight
keyIdea: Mass is how heavy something is. Measure it by balancing equal cubes until both sides level, then record a number with a unit (for example 4 cubes). Simple scales can also show grams. Bigger is not always heavier — measure, do not guess from size alone.
familyTip: Put a book on one side of a kitchen scale or homemade balance and add identical building cubes on the other until it balances. Ask: 'How many cubes is the book?' Then try a big empty box versus a small tin of beans.

visual.caption: Fair mass measure or not? Drag each clue, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: tip a balance, add cubes until level, record number+unit, reject bigger=heavier, read a scale, then challenge.

kid: Mass means how heavy something is.
Put the thing on one side of a balance. Add the same size cubes on the other side until both sides are level.
Count the cubes. Write the number and the word cubes. That is the mass in cube units.
A big balloon can be lighter than a small stone. Measure — do not trust size alone.
adult: Year 1 measure: mass/weight with non-standard units, then begin standard units (grams). Words: mass, weight, balance, heavier, lighter, cubes, grams, unit, scale.

Common mistakes: thinking bigger always means heavier; recording a number with no unit; using unequal cubes; reading the wrong mark on a scale; confusing how full something looks with how heavy it is.
In the lab your child tips a balance, adds cubes until level, records 4 cubes and grams, picks the heavier stone over a big balloon, reads a pointer at 6, then faces challenge traps for those slips.

practice.prompt: A toy balances {n} equal cubes. What mass do you record in cubes?
practice.hint: The cube count at balance is the mass in cube units.
practice.explain: Balanced with {n} cubes means the mass is {n} cubes.

practice.prompt: A bag balances {n} cubes. You add {k} more identical cubes by mistake so it tips. How many cubes were the true mass?
practice.hint: The true mass is the count that first made both sides level.
practice.explain: True mass was {n} cubes; the extra {k} tipped it past balance.

pool.prompt: Object A balances {a} cubes. Object B balances {b} cubes. How many more cubes is B than A?
